3 [10]
Choose the correct answers.
(1) [1]
Large regular long-distance bulk loads are often suited to
  1. rail transport
  2. hand carriage
  3. helicopter only
  4. bicycle courier only
(2) [1]
Drip irrigation supplies water
  1. only through river canals
  2. as seawater spray
  3. only by complete field flooding
  4. near the root zone in small quantities
(3) [1]
The main June–September rain-bearing winds are the
  1. land breeze only
  2. southwest monsoon
  3. western disturbances only
  4. polar easterlies
(4) [1]
The newer alluvium is known as
  1. Laterite
  2. Khadar
  3. Bhangar
  4. Regur
(5) [1]
Canal irrigation is favoured in much of the northern plains by
  1. permanent frost
  2. steep rocky slopes alone
  3. level land and perennial rivers
  4. absence of rivers
(6) [1]
The first step in effective waste recovery is
  1. segregation at source
  2. removing collection bins
  3. mixing all waste
  4. adding drain water
(7) [1]
The Deccan rain-shadow lies chiefly to the
  1. west of the Western Ghats in the sea
  2. north of the Himalayas
  3. east of the Western Ghats
  4. centre of the Bay of Bengal
(8) [1]
An example of renewable energy is
  1. natural gas
  2. petroleum
  3. solar energy
  4. coal
(9) [1]
Deep roots in desert plants help them to
  1. avoid minerals
  2. prevent all growth
  3. reach scarce water
  4. increase water loss
(10) [1]
Contour ploughing helps to
  1. remove soil cover
  2. eliminate all rainfall
  3. reduce runoff on slopes
  4. increase gully erosion

Part II — theory; 50 marks

Answer any 5 questions.

4 [10]
(1) [2]
A hypothetical station in the southeast coast of India has Jan–Dec temperatures (°C) [22, 24, 27, 31, 33, 30, 28, 28, 29, 28, 25, 23] and rainfall (mm) [4, 22, 4, 18, 24, 3, 3, 22, 6, 190, 136, 149]. Calculate annual temperature range and total rainfall. Identify the main wet season and infer whether summer or retreating/northeast monsoon influence is more likely, using both the rainfall pattern and the stated location.
(2) [2]
A hypothetical station in the southeast coast of India has Jan–Dec temperatures (°C) [24, 26, 29, 30, 32, 29, 27, 27, 28, 30, 27, 25] and rainfall (mm) [19, 23, 2, 2, 13, 25, 16, 13, 6, 190, 158, 190]. Calculate annual temperature range and total rainfall. Identify the main wet season and infer whether summer or retreating/northeast monsoon influence is more likely, using both the rainfall pattern and the stated location.
(3) [3]
Explain three ways the Himalayas influence India’s climate.
(4) [3]
